summary: A variance about its minimizing mean cannot bound squared deviations about every arbitrary center.
mechanism: 最小化中心扩展到任意中心

original.excerpt:
For cofactor \(i\), pad the magnitude array with zeros to length \(S_i\), and let

$$
\bar a_i=\frac{L_i}{S_i}.
$$

Then

$$
\frac{D_i}{S_i}
=
\sum_{\xi=1}^{S_i}
\bigl(|A_i(\xi)|-\bar a_i\bigr)^2,
\qquad
D_i=S_ie_i^2-L_i^2.
\tag{6.1}
$$

Restrict this sum to:

* the \(G_i\) surviving unit anchors;
* the \(N_i\) surviving complete opposite-sign pairs.

For arbitrary \(\mu\in\mathbb R\),

$$
\frac{D_i}{S_i}
\ge
G_i(1-\mu)^2
+
\sum_{p=1}^{N_i}
\left[
(r_{p,+}-\mu)^2+(r_{p,-}-\mu)^2
\right].
\tag{6.2}
$$
original.context: D_i=S_i e_i^2-L_i^2 is S_i times the squared-deviation sum about the actual mean bar(a)_i=L_i/S_i. G_i counts retained unit anchors and N_i counts retained opposite-sign pairs with magnitudes r_(p,+),r_(p,-).

witness.explanation: A variance about its minimizing mean cannot bound squared deviations about every arbitrary center.
witness.evidence: For any nonempty selected coordinate set, the right side of (6.2) grows quadratically as |mu| tends to infinity, whereas D_i/S_i is fixed and finite. As a minimal exact example, one unit coordinate has S_i=L_i=e_i^2=G_i=1 and N_i=0, so D_i/S_i=0; choosing mu=0 makes the asserted right side 1. The valid route evaluates the selected deviations at the actual mean first, then lower-bounds them by their minimum over mu.

adjudication.rationale_zh: 关于均值的方差等式被用于任意 mu。单个非零坐标即使方差为零，偏离其他中心的平方仍为正；均值条件丢失是明确的适用范围扩张。
